charts.title: 01_integrator_stiffness
charts.caption: Integrator comparison on the real 91-state BioGears sepsis extraction (60 s window; step counts extrapolated to a 48 h run). The sepsis ODE is stiff. An explicit fixed-step RK4 — the algorithm viva-hybrid's Rust engine uses — blows up for dt ≥ 0.05 s and, at steps fine enough to stay finite (down to dt = 0.001 s = 173 M steps per 48 h run), still gets the fast cardiovascular states wrong by >100× (vena-cava pressure 406 vs the true 1.6; 30/91 states off by >1%, 5 by >100%) while the slow inflammation and metabolic states track (median 0.3%). The adaptive explicit method (rk45) is stability-limited and could not finish the window. The correct solver — a stiff BDF method (CVODE) — is already compiled C inside libroadrunner and integrates the window in seconds. An independent trial (viva-hybrid) shows that even on a non-stiff model, where explicit integration is valid, a from-scratch Rust integrator beats compiled numba by only ~2×. Reimplementing the integrator is therefore not an order-of-magnitude speed lever for this model; the levers are a better/warm-started stiff solver, GPU parallelism across virtual patients, or a reduced-order surrogate.
